learning_outcomes.text: Possess and understand knowledge that provides a basis or opportunity to be original in the development and/or application of ideas, often in a research context
Students know how to apply the acquired knowledge and their problem-solving ability in new or little-known environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their field of study
Students possess the learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a largely self-directed or autonomous way

Have adequate knowledge of the scientific and technological aspects of: mathematical, analytical and numerical methods in engineering, electrical engineering, energy engineering, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, continuum mechanics, industrial electronics, automation, manufacturing, materials, quantitative management methods, industrial informatics, urban planning and infrastructures.
Perform strategic planning and apply it to both constructive and production, quality and environmental management systems.
Technically and economically manage projects, facilities, plants, companies and technological centers.
Be able to exercise general management, technical management and R&D&i project management functions in plants, companies and technological centers.
Knowledge and capabilities to organize and manage companies.
Knowledge and capabilities of strategy and planning applied to different organizational structures.
Knowledge of management information systems, industrial organization, production and logistics systems, and quality management systems.
Knowledge and capabilities for verification and control of facilities, processes and products.
Knowledge and capabilities for performing certifications, audits, verifications, tests and reports.
Know and use the main quantitative methods for business decision-making.
Model decision support systems for dealing with uncertainty.
Understand the fundamentals for auditing and certifying a Management System.
Apply the main operational tools of business management systems for process management.
Know and use the main methodologies for introducing improvements in process management.

syllabus_topics: Decision support systems in the company with uncertainty treatment. Fuzzy inference.
Quantitative methods for business decision making.
Process Management in Business Organization. Basic and advanced operational tools in process management.

assessment_methods.method: Final Project submission and presentation (Practical Block)

assessment_rules: To pass the Theoretical Block, a minimum score of 4/10 is required on the final exam. To pass the Practical Block, a minimum score of 4/10 is required for the combined activities (Laboratory Practical Deliverables and Final Project). The final grade is calculated as (0.35 × Exam Score) + (0.65 × Practical Activities Score), provided both blocks meet their minimums. If minimums are not met, the final grade will be the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0. For extraordinary examinations, the same evaluation system applies; if the Practical Block was passed in the ordinary call, its score is retained for the next two extraordinary calls.
